newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish households less pessimistic in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Swedish households less pessimistic in Feb.

text.p: Swedish households in February turned somewhat less pessimistic about economic trends in the next 12 months, according to a consumer buying survey by Statistics Sweden.

Households who believe the general economic situation in Sweden will become worse in the next 12 months decreased to 31 percent from 36 percent in January, while households who believe the situation will improve fell to 20 percent from 22 percent.
Households expected prices to rise by 1.4 percent in the next 12 months, up from 1.3 percent last month and 2.0 percent a year ago.
The consumer confidence indicator (CCI) was -9 in February, flat from January but up from -14 a year ago, Statistics Sweden said.
Regarding employment, 49 percent of households surveyed in February expected unemployment to rise in the next 12 months, down from 50 last month and flat from 49 percent a year ago.
About 14 percent saw unemployment falling, up from 12 percent both in January this year and in February 1995.
